title.undefined: AgentOSCIn — Extension of the Agentic AI Ontology

description.en: An Extension of agentO adding agentic-system orchestration, coordination & reasoning patterns, memory bindings, guardrails, human checkpoints, termination conditions, schemas, and framework-mapping properties.

title.value: AgentOSCIn — Extension of the Agentic AI Ontology

comment.undefined: A workflow step that branches based on routing logic.
Coordination pattern in which agents take turns in a fixed cyclic order.
Coordination pattern that does not match any of the predefined patterns, e.g. a framework-specific or hand-written control flow.
Coordination pattern in which agents act one after another in a fixed order, each consuming the previous output.
Coordination pattern in which agents communicate peer-to-peer along a graph of connections without a central coordinator.
Coordination pattern in which a selector — typically a model — chooses which agent speaks next at each turn.
Coordination pattern in which a manager agent delegates work to subordinate agents and integrates their results.
Coordination pattern in which agents hand off control to one another dynamically, based on which agent is best suited to continue.
Coordination pattern in which a single agent cycles between reasoning and tool execution until it produces a final answer.
A pattern of coordination among agents in a team (e.g. sequential, hierarchical, swarm).
Placeholder reasoning pattern used when the source system does not state which reasoning strategy an agent follows.
Termination condition that fires when a designated event occurs, e.g. a stop expression appearing in an agent message.
Reasoning pattern in which an agent produces explicit intermediate reasoning steps before answering.
Termination condition satisfied when the assigned task is completed.
Reasoning pattern interleaving reasoning steps with tool calls and observations (Reason + Act).
Reasoning pattern in which an agent iteratively critiques and revises its own output.
A validation, safety, or policy check applied to a task.
Termination condition that ends execution once a maximum number of turns is reached.
A structured-output schema (e.g. JSON Schema, Pydantic model).
A termination condition built by combining other conditions via a logical operator.
Termination condition under which execution ends because the routing logic reaches a terminal branch.
A complete agentic AI system encompassing one or more agents, teams, and an orchestration.
A human-in-the-loop checkpoint inserted into task execution.
Reasoning pattern that explores several alternative reasoning branches and selects among them.
A reasoning strategy adopted by an agent (e.g. chain-of-thought, ReAct, tree-of-thoughts).
A condition under which a team's execution terminates.
A reified link between a memory and the agent, team, or system that uses it, with scope and configuration.
A controller that orchestrates one or more teams to execute a workflow.
How a guardrail is implemented. Values: "FunctionBased" (a validation callable) and "LLMBased" (a natural-language validation prompt).
Specifies the schema of the structured output produced by an orchestration or task.
Combinator used to aggregate multiple predecessor steps in the source decorator (e.g. CrewAI @listen(or_(step_a, step_b)) stores "or_"). Values: "or_", "and_", or empty for single-predecessor steps.
Relates an agentic system to an agent it contains.
Framework attribute(s) the annotated element was derived from (e.g. "role, goal, backstory", "system_message", "output_pydantic"). Enables faithful regeneration of source code from the ontology.
A tool used in the execution of a task.
Kind of human interaction requested at a checkpoint. Values: "Approval", "Review", "InputRequest".
Expression or text whose occurrence triggers an event-based termination condition (e.g. a stop keyword in an agent message).
Links a workflow step to the agent that executes it (e.g. a LangGraph node function implemented by a specific LLMAgent).

Role that a prompt plays for its agent. Values: "ModelDirective" (instructs the underlying model), "OrchestratorDirective" (describes the agent to a coordinating agent), "DualDirective" (serves both purposes).

Original literal argument(s) of the framework decorator that defined this step (e.g. CrewAI @start("wait_next_run") or @listen("label")). Preserves source-level identifiers that are not method names and therefore cannot be reconstructed from the inverse of nextStep edges.
Validation performed by a guardrail: the name of the validation function, or the validation prompt for LLM-based guardrails.
Reference to the implementation of a tool, typically a module path or an "external:<name>" marker for imported tools that were not found in the parsed sources.
Associates a subject (agent, team, system) with a memory binding.
Links a memory binding to the memory it binds.
Relates an agent to the reasoning pattern it employs.
Logical operator combining the sub-conditions of a composite termination condition. Values: "OR", "AND".
Framework the agentic system was extracted from (e.g. "CrewAI", "AutoGen", "LangGraph").
Lifetime of a memory. Values: "ExecutionScoped" (discarded after the run) and "Persistent" (retained across runs).
Serialized body of the routing function that decides which branch a conditional step takes.
Number of times a task may be retried when its guardrail rejects the output.
Associates a human-in-the-loop checkpoint with a task.
Nature of the dependency between two tasks. Values: "Sequential" (ordering imposed by the workflow) and "ContextProviding" (the predecessor supplies context to the successor).
Serialized definition of a structured-output schema, expressed as JSON Schema.
A sub-condition combined within a composite termination condition.
Upper bound on the number of reasoning attempts an agent may perform before giving up.
Maximum number of conversational turns after which execution terminates.
Serialized JSON Schema describing the arguments accepted by a tool.
Relates an orchestration to the team it orchestrates.
Strategy by which a task may be handed over to another agent instead of being executed by its assigned agent.
Whether explicit reasoning is enabled for an agent.
Visibility of a memory binding. Values: "AgentPrivate" (memory owned by a single agent) and "GroupShared" (memory shared across a team).
Links a memory binding to the agent, team, or system that owns it.

JSON object mapping the return labels of a conditional step to the names of the target steps (e.g. LangGraph add_conditional_edges path map). Preserves branch targets that cannot be reconstructed from nextStep edges alone.
Where an agent's reasoning capability comes from. Values: "FrameworkManaged" (the framework adds a reasoning loop) and "ModelNative" (the underlying model reasons on its own).
Indicates that one task depends on another.
Natural-language description of the output a task is expected to produce.
Relates a team to the coordination pattern it employs.
Memory binding attached to an individual agent.
Whether the human checkpoint must be passed, i.e. execution cannot continue without human input.
Associates a guardrail with a task.
Relates a team to a termination condition that ends its execution.
Memory binding attached to a team.
Point in the execution of a task at which the human checkpoint is applied (e.g. "AfterExecution").
Framework-specific classification of an agent's role in the system. Values: "GeneralPurpose", "UserProxy", "Manager".
Relates an agentic system to a team it contains.
Key of the team/crew invoked by this workflow step (e.g. CrewAI @listen method calling crew.kickoff()). Enables per-step crew binding through the ontology round-trip.
Relates an agentic system to its orchestration.
